title: Ada and the Verdict
premise: Sebastian Hartwell, a reclusive small-town coroner who has spent years cataloguing the town's dead to avoid confronting her own buried guilt, receives two anonymous letters: one confessing to the drowning death of her childhood friend Lily Marsh twenty years ago, the other promising that more will follow unless she reopens the case. As Sebastian quietly investigates, she discovers Lily's death was no accident but a cover-up woven through the town's most respected families—including the judge who once ruled it accidental and Sebastian's own late father, who signed the report. The second letter's sender turns out to be Lily's twin sister Ada, who has returned home dying of cancer and wants the truth on record before either of them is gone. In the end, Sebastian files an amended verdict naming the killer—now a beloved local philanthropist—at the cost of her career, her safety, and the town's peace, choosing truth over the survival she'd built on silence.
about_author: O. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former rural court clerk who spent a decade transcribing verdicts in towns where everyone knew everyone's business. They write mysteries about the quiet violence small communities agree not to see.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On an ordinary morning of routine deaths and paperwork, two letters arrive—one unsigned confession to Lily Marsh's drowning, one promising 'more' if the case stays closed. Sebastian recognizes handwriting she hasn't seen in twenty years. The emotional beat is dread cracking open old grief; she must decide whether burying the past was protection or complicity.

chapters.title: The Verdict That Stood
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with interludes from Ada's letters. Pulling the original file, Sebastian finds her father's signature on a rushed ruling and discrepancies only a coroner would catch—Lily's lungs held river water, but her wrists bore marks. She visits the retired judge who closed the case; his fear confirms there was a conspiracy. Emotional beat: loyalty to her father's memory curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: What Ada Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sebastian and Ada. Sebastian traces the letter-writer to Ada Marsh, back in town under hospice care, dying and unafraid. Ada reveals what she witnessed as a child—and names Councilman Everett Voss, now the town's golden benefactor. But Voss learns they're digging, and Sebastian's office is ransacked, the file stolen. Emotional beat: alliance forged between grief-stricken women against a town that prefers its lies.

chapters.title: Amended
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With Ada's sworn testimony recorded before she weakens, Sebastian files an amended verdict naming Voss despite threats against her license and life. At a public hearing, Ada appears in a wheelchair to face him; the town fractures, some grateful, some vengeful. Ada dies days later at peace. Sebastian keeps her post, no longer invisible, guarding every grave by name. Emotional beat: costly, hard-won justice.
